attributes.body_ja:
「こそ」は、「を」や「が」に置（お）き換（か）えて使（つか）われる副助詞（ふくじょし）です。主（おも）な働（はたら）きは、文（ぶん）の中（なか）で、前（まえ）に置（お）かれた名詞（めいし）（または名詞句（めいしく））を強（つよ）く目立（めだ）たせることです。

「こそ」は、「を」や「が」が付（つ）く名詞（めいし）のあとに使（つか）われます。その名詞（めいし）が、文（ぶん）の中（なか）で特（とく）に強（つよ）く伝（つた）えたい情報（じょうほう）であるときに使（つか）います。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「こそ」は、「が」や「は」に置（お）き換（か）えることができますが、ニュアンスは「が」に近（ちか）いことが多（おお）いです。これは、「が」は特定（とくてい）の情報（じょうほう）を強調（きょうちょう）しますが、「は」は話題（わだい）を広（ひろ）く示（しめ）す働（はたら）きを持（も）つためです。理解（りかい）しやすくなるように、三（みっ）つの助詞（じょし）の違（ちが）いを次（つぎ）のように考（かんが）えてみましょう。

は - 特定（とくてい）の情報（じょうほう）を弱（よわ）く表（あらわ）す。

が - 特定（とくてい）の情報（じょうほう）を強（つよ）く表（あらわ）す。

こそ - 特定（とくてい）の情報（じょうほう）をとても強（つよ）く表（あらわ）す。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「こそ」には、名前（なまえ）などの固有名詞（こゆうめいし）のあとに使（つか）う使（つか）い方（かた）もあります。これは、ほかの人（ひと）からお礼（れい）を言（い）われたり、謝（あやま）られたりしたときに、話（はな）し手（て）が自分（じぶん）も同（おな）じように（または、それよりももっと強（つよ）く）感（かん）じていると言（い）いたいときに使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
こそ is an adverbial particle in Japanese that primarily replaces either を or が. Its main role is to highlight the preceding noun (or noun phrase) as being the most important piece of information in relation to the rest of the sentence. In English, this is an effect that is primarily achieved through things like bold text, underlining, or emphasizing a particular word in speech. If we were to make a direct comparison to an English statement, then things like 'precisely because it's (A)', or 'rather it is due to (A)', are quite similar to こそ's function.

こそ can be used directly after any noun that would usually take the を, or が particles, so long as that particular piece of information needs to be emphasized.

Caution

Although こそ is able to replace が or は, the nuance will usually come across as more similar to が, due to the fact that が puts emphasis on a specific point, while は nominates general topics. To make things easier, the three particles can be thought of in the following way:

は- Weakly highlights specific information.

が- Strongly highlights specific information.

こそ- Very strongly highlights specific information.

Fun Fact

こそ is often used after names or pronouns, as a way to reply to thanks/apologies. In these situations, it expresses that the speaker feels equally (or more) obliged to say what was just said to them by someone else.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese
A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns
A Dictionary of Intermediate Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both structures single out and highlight something, but in different ways. のはXの方だ highlights contrast between options and is often used in apologies, e.g. 悪いのは僕の方だ ('I'm the one that's at fault.') こそ emphasizes exclusivity or importance, e.g. 私こそ謝るべきだ ('I, and no one else, should apologize.')

attributes.body: Both add emphasis, but with opposite nuance. なんか・なんて often downplays or dismisses, while こそ highlights importance or exclusivity. The former can feel self-deprecating or casual, while the latter stresses that something uniquely applies. Compare 私なんかできるのかな？ ('I wonder if someone like me could do it?') versus 彼こそできる ('Him, if no one else, can do it.')

second_relatable.title: こそ

attributes.body: Both use こそ for emphasis, but からこそ highlights a reason or cause, meaning 'precisely because', e.g. 努力したからこそできた ('I could do it precisely because I worked hard.'). こそ on its own emphasizes the word it follows, framing it as precisely the one, e.g. 彼こそできる ('He, if no one else, can do it.')

attributes.body: より expresses a general comparison, like 'more than (A)' or '~er,' e.g. 月曜日より水曜日がいい ('Wednesday is better than Monday.') or 走るより野球をするのが好き ('I prefer playing baseball to running.'). In contrast, こそ adds emphasis, highlighting something as especially important, e.g. 月曜日こそ図書館に行きたい ('Monday is precisely when I want to go to the library.').

second_relatable.title: こそ
second_relatable.meaning: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text

attributes.body: Both involve the same こそ, but one attaches to nouns and the other to verb + て form. こそ emphasizes a specific word or element, often to contrast or highlight, e.g. 彼こそできる ('He, if nobody else, can do it.'). In contrast, ～てこそ focuses a condition that must be met for something to be true, e.g. 大人になってこそ分かる 'understand only after becoming an adult'.

second_relatable.title: ～てこそ
second_relatable.meaning: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until

attributes.body: こそ and なら can look similar after a noun, e.g. 彼こそできる vs. 彼ならできる, but differ in nuance. こそ is emphatic, suggesting that something someone is 'the one', e.g. 彼こそできる ('He's exactly the one who can do it.'). なら implies a conditional focus, e.g. 彼ならできる ('If it's him we're talking about, he can do it.'), without the nuance of excluding other possibilities that こそ can have.

second_relatable.title: なら
second_relatable.meaning: Were it, If, If it's the case, As for (Conditional)

attributes.body: Both express emphasis, but in different ways. あまり is a noun that emphasizes an extreme degree leading to an unintended result, e.g. 悲しみのあまり泣き出した ('She burst into tears from too much sadness.') こそ is a particle that stresses importance or exclusivity, e.g. 今日こそ早く寝よう ('Today, for sure, I'll go to bed early.')
